items.text: Prospective multi‑domain 18‑month trajectories can reveal asynchrony in language, participation, and QoL recovery; descriptive and epistemic value remains even if the final clinical prediction tool is not successful.
Fine‑grained recording, training, and verification of treatment content/dose across inpatient and community settings go beyond billed time and provide clinically usable associative knowledge.
Comparing imaging/candidate genetic markers with routine clinical information incrementally can explore individual differences without claiming to have proven biological mechanisms.
Observational treatment exposure is confounded by severity, access, and temporal changes; association and trajectory tools cannot directly infer causal effects of treatment dose.

With 100 subjects, single‑center imaging, and candidate gene interactions, the dimensionality is too large; screening must be placed inside internal resampling, CV after fixing the final variable set will be optimistically biased, and MCID does not equate to clinical predictive validity.

Consent/testing requirements, loss to follow‑up, and the 3–4 hour assessment burden may exclude severe cases and make MAR untenable; existing support, communication, and retention measures should be acknowledged.
